review: 2:1 נִשְׂגָּב בְּמִדּוֹת — 'sublime in attributes'; the Arabic السَّجَايَا is 'traits', and מִדּוֹת is the standard Hebrew term for God's attributes without adding a syllable.
3:2 הָיָה לִפְנֵי הָרִים — Proverbs 8:25 (בְּטֶרֶם הָרִים הָטְבָּעוּ); the Arabic قَبْلَ الْجِبَال is that verse, and Hebrew keeps the mountains as the marker of eternity.
4:2 בַּעַל חֶסֶד — 'possessor of grace'; בַּעַל in construct is biblical (בַּעַל חֵמָה, Prov 29:22), and the glossary note about בַּעַל sounding like 'Baal' applies here too.
5:2 שֶׁמֶשׁ צֶדֶק — Malachi 3:20 (שֶׁמֶשׁ צְדָקָה), for شَمْسُ الْبِرّ; the construct is kept even though the Arabic has an apposition.
